bibl.title: Simple statistical identification and removal of contaminant sequences in marker-gene and metagenomics data

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: contaminant DNA in marker-gene and metagenomic sequencing - sequences that are in the data and not in the sample - and how to identify them without knowing in advance what they are
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: whether contaminant sequences can be separated from true community members de novo, using only statistical patterns already present in a standard sequencing run
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: decontam: two independent classifiers built on two reproduced signatures of contamination - inverse correlation with DNA concentration, and higher prevalence in negative controls - released as an R package
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: method
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: contamination that survives good laboratory practice and is invisible to the quality control usually used to detect it, biasing hardest exactly where biomass is lowest and the claims are most contested
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: a two-component mixture model of contaminant and sample DNA, turned into two score statistics and a user-set classification threshold, validated on an oral dataset, a dilution series and two published low-biomass studies
span.term: a two-component mixture model of contaminant and sample DNA, turned into two score statistics and a user-set classification threshold, validated on an oral dataset, a dilution series and two published low-biomass studies
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: contaminant DNA enters at roughly constant absolute concentration while sample DNA varies, so as a proportion of the total the contaminant's frequency falls as sample concentration rises - a slope of -1 in log space against a slope of 0
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: with no competing sample DNA, a negative control's sequencing capacity is available to whatever contaminant is present, so contaminants are detected in a larger fraction of controls than of true samples
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: because the frequency method reads low sample concentration as evidence of contamination, any real sequence that is genuinely commoner in low-biomass samples presents with the contaminant signature - so mixing environments manufactures false positives out of true biology
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: decontam is not designed for cross-contamination, which violates its founding assumption that contaminants and true members are distinct populations
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the frequency method's approximations break down in exactly the low-biomass regime where contamination matters most - when contaminants are a large fraction of reads
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: applying it across environments of systematically different biomass can classify real sequences as contaminants, because low concentration is the contaminant signature
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: it depends on patterns across samples, so it has low sensitivity for contaminants present in very few samples - the tail it cannot see
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the default classification threshold is not recommended as-is: the authors direct users to read a threshold off their own score histogram instead
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the method is less effective when groups of samples carry systematically different contaminant patterns, which is why batches must be declared by the user rather than detected
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: model comparison by ratio of sums-of-squared-residuals, carried from linear regression into a per-sequence classifier - and deliberately stripped of the inferential guarantee it carries in its home field
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: a two-component mixture model, carried from statistical modelling to represent total DNA as contaminant plus sample
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the field's standard check that a negative control shows no band on an agarose gel, taken as evidence that contamination is absent
span.note: eliminates: contamination in the sequencing library - and the paper's own sentence says this check does NOT eliminate it, because band-less samples still generate non-negligible reads · outcome: absent-stated-about-other
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: removing every sequence that appears in a negative control
span.note: eliminates: contaminant sequences - and it OVER-removes, because cross-contamination puts abundant TRUE sequences into the negative controls · outcome: absent-stated-about-other
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: discarding sequences below an ad hoc relative abundance threshold
span.note: eliminates: abundant contaminants, which it fails to remove, while removing rare features that are truly present in the sample · outcome: absent-stated-about-other
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: excluding taxa on a blacklist of previously reported contaminants
span.note: eliminates: previously reported contaminants - leaving study-specific contaminants in place and removing true sequences · outcome: absent-stated-about-other
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: cross-checking taxonomic assignments against a second controlled vocabulary, HOMD against SILVA, at the genus level
span.note: eliminates: a contaminant call that is an artefact of one reference vocabulary's genus boundaries · outcome: partial
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: an explicit `ambiguous` class for genera that neither reference database resolves, instead of forcing every genus into contaminant or oral
span.note: eliminates: a genus with no evidence either way being forced into `contaminant` or `oral` and counted as if it had been decided · outcome: held
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: turning the method on a published low-biomass claim - the placenta microbiome - where the expected answer was already contested
span.note: eliminates: a decontamination method validated only on data where the right answer was chosen by the people validating it · outcome: held
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.
